title: Vertex tangent frames for normal mapping
purpose: Compute the vec4 tangent attribute three.js uses for normal maps from positions, normals, UVs and indices: angle-weighted tangents along increasing u, made perpendicular to the normal, with w = -1 where UVs are mirrored and a stable fallback for degenerate UVs. Use it for normal-mapped procedural and imported meshes.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: computeVertexTangents needs no three.js; addTangents takes three.js as THREE and sets the tangent attribute; only 0.186.1 was run.

exports.name: computeVertexTangents
exports.signature: computeVertexTangents(positions, normals, uvs, indices = null, options = {}) -> Float32Array
exports.summary: x, y, z, w per vertex: the unit tangent along increasing u and the handedness of the bitangent.

exports.name: addTangents
exports.summary: Set the geometry's tangent attribute (itemSize 4) from its position, normal, uv and index.

inputs.normals: unit x, y, z per vertex
inputs.indices: triangle indices, or null for a triangle soup

options.name: orthogonalize
options.meaning: Remove the normal's component from each tangent (Gram-Schmidt).

limits: Tangents are averaged per vertex from angle-weighted face directions; this is not the MikkTSpace algorithm, so a normal map baked in a tool that uses MikkTSpace can show faint seams or shading differences, most of all on low-poly meshes. Vertices shared across a UV seam or a mirror line average both sides; split them first (as UV seams usually already are). The handedness is per vertex, so a triangle whose corners disagree shades with a crease. Degenerate UVs get an arbitrary perpendicular. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Per-triangle tangent and bitangent from UV deltas (Lengyel)
Bitangent handedness as the sign of cross(N, T) . B
